newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond presses on, US helps.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia 10-yr bond presses on, US helps.

text.p: *The June Australian 10-year bond futures contract extended
Friday's short end-led rally during after hours trading as U.S.
Treasuries remained buoyed by foreign demand.

The June Australian 10-year bond futures contract extended Friday's short end-led rally during after hours trading as U.S. Treasuries remained buoyed by foreign demand and hopes that economy will show moderation.
The contract ended SYCOM at it highest level since February at 92.590, up from a pit close of 92.540, and overcoming Friday's dayside peak of 92.570.

Analysts expect the contract could be restrained to a 92.550/92.620 range with the market likely to be held by the already tight Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread, but the solid break of 92.500 should see it press the 92.700s soon.
Three-year bonds and bill futures remained around Friday's strong gains which followed a weak April retail trade report, which fuelled talk of the possibility of a further monetary policy easing.

June three-year bonds, which ended SYCOM unchanged from its 93.78 pit close, are likely to retest Friday's intra-day 93.83 peak, but the contract is now registering overbought levels with a relative strength index of over 75 percent, analysts noted.
April building approvals are due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) and are forecast to rise 3.0 percent after falling in four of the last five months, according to a Reuters survey.
